Q1_cancel_join_thread_semantics_all_call.assessment: PASS — abandonment is safe at every caller; no reader can depend on abandoned contents

the parent NEVER reads the inbox: puts only (dispatch 408, close sentinels 423, rehydration 790/793); the only inbox reader is the worker loop (worker.py pool_main: get until None), and cancel() terminates those workers
the only ready-queue reader is start(); in the failure path start() has long completed; in the start-failure paths the notes are abandoned by design

committed work is journal-backed, never inbox-backed: rows are journalled by the parent only after the synchronous outbox recv (_journal_row under the run loop); abandoned inbox jobs are uncommitted rows that resume re-runs; results already in the SimpleQueue pipe but unrecv'd are likewise uncommitted (the serial-parity prefix comes from _attach_rows over recv'd outcomes)
the OLD ordering preserved nothing of value on these paths: with workers terminated, queued jobs had no consumer in any ordering — the only thing the old ordering 'delivered' was the wedge itself
cancel_join_thread only sets the shared no-join flag; it does not break puts, kill feeders, or affect gets — the workers are terminated moments later regardless
